notes.text: Re-teach that softmax preserves sum-to-1 while amplifying differences by working through [2,1,0] to show the largest stays largest.
Build on accurate dot-product calculation and same-direction interpretation to frame attention scores as similarity before softmax.
Have the learner apply row-wise softmax to the correct 5x5 QK^T to show each row sums to 1 yet stays peaked.
Next time contrast scaling versus softmax by pointing to the learner's correct formula and asking which operation creates probabilities versus controls magnitude.
Next time build on the correct divide-by-8 for d_k=64 to teach that scaling prevents large dot-products from saturating softmax.
Next time re-check softmax sharpness by computing exp(4)/(exp(4)+1) ~0.98 to confront the 0.8 estimate for scores [4,0].

links.why: Learner attributed softmax's probability normalization role to the scaling division.

notes.text: Re-teach why sinusoidal encodings use many frequencies to capture relative position at multiple scales, since the learner knows attention is order-blind but chose faster training as the reason.
Build on the learner's correct variance-64 and sharper-softmax answers to have them derive the 1/sqrt(d_k) rescaling next time.
Build on the correct 64-dim calculation and different-patterns idea by asking the learner to explain how heads are concatenated and projected next time.
Have the learner hand-compute softmax for [10,1,1,1] to confront the 40% estimate and see the top token approaches 100%.
Push the partial batch-size answer next time to articulate per-token normalization and variable sequence length as the reason for layer norm.
Use the solid cross-entropy results for p=0.25 and p going to 0 to link confident softmax outputs to low loss.
Next time confront the idea that queries come from values by having the learner trace where the single current-step query comes from versus reused past keys and values.
Re-check KV-cache sizing by having the learner explicitly multiply 2 for K and V times layers times d_model times bytes, since the answer was half the correct size.
Build on the correct one-token-at-a-time and causal-mask counting to explain why all past keys and values must stay cached while only one query is needed.
Have the learner plug y_i near 1 into their own y_i - y_i^2 formula to see why saturated softmax gradients vanish.
Re-ask the learner to explain why the softmax Jacobian has negative off-diagonal terms since they left it blank after seeing the solution.
Use the learner's correct chain-rule and wasted-head answers to trace how saturated attention in one head limits gradient flow to earlier weights.
Next time build on the learner's correct recall that the N x N matrix is the memory bottleneck and FlashAttention avoids storing it to introduce how tiling keeps it in SRAM.
Re-teach online softmax with running max and rescaled denominator because the learner proposed averaging per-tile softmaxes.
Re-check that FlashAttention is exact, not approximate, by contrasting exact recomputation with approximation methods.
Re-practice grouped-query cache sizing as 32/8 = 4x smaller because the learner answered 8x.
